rows.expected: Logical offsets strongly reduce position-reset error.
rows.observed: Layer-0 RMSE became exactly zero and final-layer RMSE fell in 10/10 paired runs.
rows.interpretation: Source-relative continuity is not a RoPE-only effect.

rows.expected: The offset-effect direction survives the small-model increase.
rows.observed: All small-model mechanisms reached zero layer-0 RMSE and improved final-layer RMSE in 15/15 pairs.
rows.interpretation: The representation result is not confined to the tiny mechanism microscope.

rows.expected: Offsets often improve 8L natural-text loss, but contextualization may dominate.
rows.observed: Offsets improved final-layer K RMSE in 30/30 pairs, but improved loss in only 5/30 pairs.
rows.interpretation: Representation fidelity does not guarantee lower next-token loss.
rows.thesis_effect: strengthens factor separation but weakens a direct quality claim

rows.expected: Offsets improve fidelity while routing and composition remain limiting.
rows.observed: Routed loss improved in 35/60 pairs; learned-absolute and sinusoidal improved on average, whereas RoPE worsened in both datasets and tiers.
rows.interpretation: Position repair is necessary mechanistically but routing/composition and training distribution control utility.

rows.expected: Overlap can recover context, but need not improve every mechanism or seed.
rows.observed: Overlap consistently reduced representation error, while task effects were small or mixed across domains.
rows.interpretation: Contextualization and task utility remain distinct from coordinate repair.
